title: Sustainable Farming and Natural Wine
quiz.0.question: In Italy, which sustainable practice has the unified EU "Euro Leaf" certification and the clearest rules?
quiz.0.explanation: Organic wine (vino biologico) has unified EU rules and the Euro Leaf certification, which ban synthetic chemicals in the vineyard and set limits on sulphur dioxide added during winemaking.
quiz.1.question: Besides organic farming, what core idea does biodynamics stress?
quiz.1.options.0: Fermentation must take place in amphorae
quiz.1.options.1: Seeing the vineyard as a self-sustaining ecosystem and farming by astronomical cycles and special preparations (such as horn manure)
quiz.1.options.2: A total ban on adding any sulphur dioxide at bottling
quiz.1.options.3: Only native Italian grapes may be grown
quiz.1.explanation: Biodynamics is based on Rudolf Steiner's philosophy, stressing the influence of the cosmos on plants and using specific preparations to enliven the soil and strengthen the vines' resilience.
quiz.2.question: Friuli in north-eastern Italy, and especially pioneers such as Josko Gravner, are world-famous for reviving which ancient winemaking technique?
quiz.2.options.0: Making sparkling wine by the Charmat method
quiz.2.options.1: Making sweet wine from dried grapes (appassimento)
quiz.2.options.2: Fermenting white grapes on their skins in clay vessels (qvevri/amphora) to make orange wine
quiz.2.options.3: Ageing white wine in 100% new small French oak
quiz.2.explanation: Josko Gravner and others brought in clay vessels from Georgia and fermented white grapes (such as Ribolla Gialla) on their skins for long periods, creating amber orange wines with tannin — a milestone of the modern natural-wine movement.
quiz.3.question: Which statement about "natural wine" is most accurate?
quiz.3.options.0: Natural wine has strict, unified official certification worldwide
quiz.3.options.1: The core idea of natural wine is "nothing added, nothing taken away", usually fermented with wild yeasts and with little or no added sulphur dioxide
quiz.3.options.2: Natural wine must have large amounts of cultured yeast added during fermentation to ensure it ferments
quiz.3.options.3: Natural wine must be strictly fined and filtered before bottling
quiz.3.explanation: The core philosophy of natural wine is minimal intervention ("nothing added, nothing taken away"): wild yeasts, no fining or filtration, and very little sulphur dioxide. It currently lacks a unified official certification worldwide.
slides.0.title: Sustainable Farming and Natural Wine
slides.0.subtitle: Italy leads Europe's sustainable wine revolution: from organic to natural wine
slides.1.title: Italy: A Leader of Sustainable Farming in Europe
slides.1.content:
Italy is not only one of the world's largest wine producers but also a pioneer of sustainable farming. Its favourable climate (especially the dry, breezy conditions of the centre and south) makes it easier than in Europe's damper areas to reduce the use of chemical treatments.

>18%of vineyards certified organic, far above the global average
Demeterbiodynamic pioneers, adopted by top estates such as Foradori and Alois Lageder
Vini VeriItaly is the most important driving force and fair hub of the global natural-wine movement
Mainstreamsustainability has deeply influenced top areas such as Barolo, Brunello and Chianti Classico
slides.2.title: Three Sustainable Approaches: Organic, Biodynamic, Natural
slides.2.content:
Organic wine

The entry-level certification with the clearest rules

Certification: the EU organic logo (Euro Leaf)
Rules: synthetic fertilisers, herbicides and insecticides banned in the vineyard
Winemaking: stricter limits on added sulphur dioxide (SO2) than ordinary wine
Features: currently the category with the most complete rules and widest uptake; over 18% of Italy's vineyards qualify

Biodynamic

The philosophically deepest evolution of organic

Certification: Demeter or Biodyvin
Philosophy: Rudolf Steiner's ideas — seeing the vineyard as a self-sustaining ecosystem
Practices: using "preparations" (such as preparation 500, horn manure) to enliven the soil; scheduling work by lunar and astronomical cycles
Features: stresses strengthening the vine's own resilience and the expression of terroir; uptake among top estates is growing fast

Natural wine

The most radical philosophy of minimal intervention

Certification: no unified official rules; promoted by private associations such as Vinnatur and Triple A
Philosophy: "Nothing added, nothing taken away"
Practices: organic/biodynamic farming required; wild yeasts only; no fining or filtration; little or no added SO2
Features: often cloudy with oxidative notes, variable in quality — the most controversial category
slides.3.title: Biodynamics in Practice: Preparation 500 and the Biodynamic Calendar
slides.3.content:
🐄 Preparation 500 (the core tool)

Horn manure

Cow manure is packed into cow horns and buried over winter to ferment; in spring it is dug up, stirred in water (dynamisation) and sprayed on the soil; it is believed to enliven soil microbes and encourage deeper roots

🌙 The Biodynamic Calendar

Scheduling work by the position of the moon

Root days: soil work; flower days: thought to favour floral expression; leaf days: avoid major interventions; fruit days: suited to harvesting and considered the best days for tasting

🌿 A leading Italian estate

Foradori (Trentino)

Elisabetta Foradori is one of Italy's biodynamic pioneers; her Teroldego wines show how biodynamics lets local grapes express their terroir more fully

🏔️ Alois Lageder (Alto Adige)

Fully biodynamic certification

Alois Lageder practises complete biodynamics in the cool climate of Alto Adige and is seen as the highest standard of sustainable farming in northern Italy
slides.4.title: The Orange-Wine Revival: Friuli's Pioneering Spirit
slides.4.content:
Friuli-Venezia Giulia is the birthplace of the modern orange-wine (skin-fermented white) revival, and two legendary figures defined this revolution

📍 The area (Friuli Collio / Carso): in north-eastern Italy on the border with Slovenia, winemakers revived the ancient amphora winemaking of the Caucasus, macerating white grapes on their skins for long periods — the very definition of modern orange wine
👨‍🍳 Pioneer Josko Gravner: abandoned modern stainless steel and travelled to Georgia to bring back large clay vessels (qvevri), macerating white Ribolla Gialla on its skins for months to make deep-coloured orange wines with tannin and complex oxidative aromas; he became a spiritual leader of the global natural-wine movement
🍷 Legend Radikon: the late Stanko Radikon insisted on long skin maceration and no added sulphur, and bottled in special 500 ml or 1000 ml narrow-necked bottles to reduce oxygen contact; his wines are now regarded as natural-wine textbooks
🎨 Orange-wine style: amber to orange colour; aromas of dried apricot, black tea, honey, nuts and spice; a palate combining red-wine-like tannic structure with the fresh acidity of a white; one of the most characterful wines to pair with modern cuisine
slides.5.title: Key Takeaways
slides.5.points.0: Over 18% of Italy's vineyards are certified organic, making it a leader in sustainable farming in Europe
slides.5.points.1: Three levels of certification: organic (Euro Leaf, the clearest rules) → biodynamic (Demeter, deeper philosophy) → natural wine (Vinnatur, minimal intervention)
slides.5.points.2: Organic wine bans synthetic pesticides and strictly limits added sulphur dioxide; it is currently the most widespread sustainable certification
slides.5.points.3: Biodynamics is based on Rudolf Steiner's philosophy; preparation 500 (horn manure) is the core tool for enlivening the soil
slides.5.points.4: The biodynamic calendar divides days into root, flower, leaf and fruit days; "fruit days" are considered best for harvesting and tasting
slides.5.points.5: Orange wine = white grapes fermented on their skins, a white with tannin; Friuli is the birthplace of its modern revival
slides.5.points.6: Josko Gravner brought in Georgian qvevri, and Radikon insisted on no added SO2 — the two godfathers of the global orange-wine revolution
slides.5.points.7: The core philosophy of natural wine: "nothing added, nothing taken away", relying on wild yeasts, without fining or filtration
